issues.description: The problem statement/UML specify orderMeal(Meal): void (a method with no return value), but the solution implementation declares orderMeal(Meal) as returning boolean. This is a signature mismatch: students reading the UML/text will implement a void method while the reference solution uses a boolean return. This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected method contract and may cause test or grading mismatches.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the method signature consistent. Either change the solution to match the specification by declaring orderMeal as void (public void orderMeal(Meal meal)) and remove boolean return values, or update the problem statement/UML to indicate the method returns a boolean and document its meaning. The preferred fix to match the UML/spec: modify the solution's method signature to 'public void orderMeal(Meal meal)' and adjust the implementation to not return a value (e.g., drop the boolean return and simply perform the enqueue/check logic).
